title: Surgical region fail + gradual GPU depletion chaos harness for SLO breakpoint testing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build and validate a targeted fault-injection harness that exercises two correlated failure modes we see in production: (1) a surgical region egress/network partition that causes request routing loss for 10-30 minutes, and (2) progressive GPU pool exhaustion in a secondary region (gradual node drain rather than instant blackhole). We will measure how our routing, circuit breakers, and load-shedding policies influence SLOs (p95 latency, availability) and error budgets. The harness should be reusable, parameterizable, and produce dashboards/traceable artifacts for postmortem and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Inject simulated region egress partition for region-us-west-2 while keeping control-plane healthy
Simulate progressive GPU depletion in region-us-east-1 by taking 10%, then 30%, then 70% of pool capacity offline over 20 minutes
Observe routing fallback to secondary models/regions and validate circuit-breaker behavior does not cascade retries
Collect golden signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue lengths, token cost) and produce a baseline comparison report
Automated playbook triggers: when p95 > 400ms or error_rate > 2% for 5m, verify load-shedding policy triggers and traffic is rerouted according to policy
Document required tuned CB thresholds and updated runbook snippets for on-call
One end-to-end GitHub PR with harness code and a corresponding Grafana dashboard link merged and deployed to staging
test_plan_steps: Step 0: Create isolated staging deployment with two regions: us-west-2 and us-east-1 and instrument synthetic clients
Step 1: Baseline run for 60 minutes capturing normal SLO metrics
Step 2: Induce a 12-minute egress partition on us-west-2 using network policy simulator (drop 100% egress to public clients)
Step 3: Simultaneously, schedule progressive GPU drain on us-east-1: remove 10% capacity at T+2m, 30% at T+8m, 70% at T+20m
Step 4: Monitor routing decisions, ended requests, circuit breaker trips, and client retry patterns; ensure clients receive 503s or fallbacks instead of prolonged timeouts
Step 5: Run a second iteration with the same fault profile but with conservative vs aggressive load-shedding to assess trade-offs
Step 6: Aggregate traces, tokens, cost, and latency to generate the resilience report
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Infra, Serving Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on staging topology and required dashboards.
2026-03-04: PoC harness committed to branch feature/eng-93021-harness. Basic network partition injector implemented using chaos-proxy shim.
2026-03-06: First synthetic run completed. Observed unexpected retry amplification when circuit-breaker window was 60s. Collected traces and linked to issue ENG-93100 for retry-safety investigation.

2026-03-08: Tuned circuit-breaker rollout: lowered failure threshold and shortened sliding window; re-ran tests and saw a 35% reduction in client-facing errors but increased token reroutes. Drafted runbook changes.
2026-03-10: Draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2895. Attaching Grafana dashboard snapshot for comparison: grafana.redwood.dev/d/chaos/eng-93021-summary
decisions_and_tradeoffs: We chose a progressive GPU drain pattern instead of instant preemption because it better mirrors observed production degradation (nodes becoming overloaded then OOM). Tradeoff: longer experiment time and more complex signal correlation vs higher fidelity results. We are testing both conservative load-shedding (preferred for user-facing SLAs) and aggressive load-shedding (preferred for cost protection) to produce concrete guidance for policy tuning.
risks: Staging topology divergence from production could hide routing edge-cases
Synthetic clients may not reproduce backpressure amplification from real customers
Inter-team coordination risk: Dedicated team must approve simulated node drains
next_actions: Review PR #2895 with Runtime team and address comments from SRE by 2026-03-12
Coordinate a cross-team run on 2026-03-18 with Dedicated capacity owners for controlled node drains
Publish final resilience report and update runbook by 2026-03-24
notes: Early runs uncovered that the KV cache warmed differently under progressive drain which increased cold-start token costs in fallback regions; adding a cache-prefetch stage to the harness is recommended. Also capturing sample prompts to run quality regressions against fallback model variants. Monitor cost delta per token during experiments to inform Optimize recommendations.
